title: Arsenal vs. Everton: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray8:30 PM EDTArsenal vs. Everton has been an ever-present Premier League fixture for the past 34 years. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesArsenal face their 226th match against Everton when returning to Premier League action at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners, fresh from their 2–2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, are aiming to keep within touching distance of Manchester City, who currently lead the standings by three points. Hard-fought victories over Leeds United and Nottingham Forest since the international break haven’t been enough to usurp the perfect Cityzens.

Meanwhile, Everton journey to north London off the back of their first defeat of the campaign at the hands of Chelsea, and David Moyes will demand a more resilient performance this time around. The Toffees have only won two of their seven Premier League matches, but they would be thrilled to add to a collection of four draws when facing Arsenal.

Mikel Arteta, who represented both clubs during his playing career, knows his players will have to improve in the final third if they’re to overcome a stubborn defense. The defending champions managed just one shot on target during their unspectacular 1–0 win at the City Ground last weekend, with a more polished display required in front of their own supporters.

Arsenal are strong favorites for this one. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesThere’s little time for Arsenal to rest as their hectic October continues. They have already played four matches since the international break concluded, and the Everton clash is the first of five more games before the next hiatus in November.

But Arteta’s squad depth has allowed him to navigate the busy calendar with few issues, with the Spaniard able to rotate personnel against Everton without reducing the quality of his starting lineup. That’s a luxury Moyes simply doesn’t possess.

This encounter is unlikely to be filled with goal-mouth action considering the impressive defensive records and tame attacking returns of both teams in the Premier League this season. The more efficient side should enjoy the greater success—and that’s almost certain to be Arsenal.
The Gunners have the superior roster, greater confidence and home advantage for the upcoming duel.
Arsenal will continue without the injured duo of William Saliba and Christos Tzolis, while Piero Hincapié could sit out another match following the ankle injury sustained in his post-Leeds warm-down.

However, the big disappointment for Arsenal is the quad injury sustained by Bukayo Saka against Bayern midweek, with the Englishman lasting just 10 minutes before being replaced. Arteta confessed that “it doesn’t look good at all” for Saka after the match, and some reports have suggested he may be missing for around two months.
Noni Madueke will take over from Saka on the right-hand side after scoring the winning goal against Forest last Sunday. Eberechi Eze, who netted at Bayern, will line up on the other flank.
Ben White and Myles Lewis-Skelly might be optional changes made by Arteta, who will be keen to keep his team as fresh as possible against an Everton team which didn’t play midweek.
Arsenal predicted lineup vs. Everton (4-2-3-1): Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Lewis-Skelly; Madueke, Ødegaard, Eze; Havertz.
Everton’s XI has been settled for much of the season and any changes from the Chelsea defeat will be subtle. Moyes is fortunate to have an entirely healthy squad for the trip to the capital.

Thierno Barry will be aiming to continue his strong goalscoring form, supported by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall in the No. 10 position. Behind the Englishman will be his compatriots James Garner and Harrison Armstrong, with Jack Grealish on the left wing.

The defense should be unchanged from last weekend, meaning Ainsley Maitland-Niles will line up against his former side at right back. Christian Nørgaard could also feature from the bench against the club he departed over the summer.
Jordan Pickford will be tasked with keeping out a number of his England teammates at the Emirates.
Everton predicted lineup vs. Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong; Röhl, Dewsbury-Hall, Grealish; Barry.
